title: Cauliflower 'potato' salad
summary: A picnic-style faux potato salad: tender cauliflower with chopped egg, celery and dill pickle in a mustardy mayonnaise dressing.
steps: Boil the florets in salted water for 5–6 minutes, until tender but still holding their shape. Drain, spread on a tray and cool completely; warm cauliflower thins the dressing.
Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt, pepper and dill in a large bowl.
Pat the cauliflower dry and fold it into the dressing with the eggs, celery, pickle and onion.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour. Stir, taste for salt, and dust with paprika before serving.
tips: Slightly overcooking a few of the florets gives the creamy, broken-edged texture of real potato salad.

origin.history: Potato salad came to the United States largely with German immigrants in the 1800s, whose versions were dressed warm with vinegar and bacon. The cold, mayonnaise-dressed style with egg and pickle became an American picnic and barbecue staple in the twentieth century. Using cauliflower in place of potato is a modern low-carb adaptation.
